16 / ANALYTICAL

Answers begin with better analysis.

Not every material question fits a standard assay. Analytical as a Service creates a starting point for discussing a defined technical question: which material is involved, what decision the information should support, which evidence is already available, and what type of analysis may be appropriate. The scope and available methods are agreed for each enquiry.

THE SERVICE IN CONTEXT

A defined scope leads to a better decision.

Explore analytical questions involving composition, identity, properties and data interpretation across valuable materials.

The suitable approach depends on the material, the intended outcome and the details agreed by the parties.

A CLOSER LOOK

What deserves attention.

Different specimen forms and questions call for different considerations. The following themes help frame the discussion.

01

Start with the decision, not an instrument

A useful analytical brief explains whether the purpose is material identification, comparison between lots, an impurity profile, compositional screening, specification checking or an investigation of an unexpected result. The intended decision helps determine sampling needs, method suitability and how much detail is meaningful.

02

Elemental and chemical composition

Chemical analysis can investigate major constituents, trace elements or impurities in ores, concentrates, precious metals and other relevant materials. Results must be understood alongside the actual sample form, preparation history, calibration approach and reporting limits. No single technique answers every elemental question.

03

Mineral and ore characterisation

For geological specimens, the distinction between bulk composition and the minerals present can be important. Representative sampling, particle-size variation, heterogeneity and preparation are often as consequential as the eventual measurement. Characterisation may involve multiple complementary observations rather than one definitive number.

04

Gold, alloys and precious-metal questions

Precious-metal analysis may focus on content, alloy composition, fineness, impurities or variation across a lot. A surface reading and an examination of a representative portion may answer different questions. Interpretation should make clear which item or portion a result describes.

05

Diamonds, gemstones and material identification

Identification and characterisation of stones may combine visual, optical, physical and, where suitable, instrumental evidence. Identity, treatment, synthetic origin, grading and geographic provenance are separate questions. Conclusions should match the competence, specimens and methods actually involved.

06

Method suitability, quality and transparent reporting

Examples of techniques used within the wider analytical industry include XRF, ICP-based analysis, fire assay, microscopy and optical or vibrational spectroscopy. These are method examples, not a statement that ASL operates every instrument in-house. A proposed scope should identify what will be measured, which test method will be used, what sample preparation is required, and how limitations and findings will be communicated.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

What to prepare.

A few useful details can make your first enquiry much more focused.

  • Material type, form, approximate quantity and number of samples
  • The business or scientific decision the result should support
  • Elements, compounds, properties or characteristics of interest
  • Known source, prior handling and sampling procedure, where available
  • Existing reports, drawings, specifications or comparison samples
  • Relevant detection-limit, reporting-unit or documentation needs
  • Handling hazards, preferred location and any timing constraints

COMMON QUESTIONS

A little more clarity.

Is Analytical as a Service the same as a gold or mineral assay?+
An assay generally addresses a defined measurement of a material. A broader analytical enquiry may include identity, composition, material characterisation, comparison, interpretation or several related questions. The right scope depends on the specimen and purpose.
Can I request a specific laboratory technique?+
Yes. Mention a preferred method or a relevant standard when enquiring. Its suitability and actual availability must be confirmed before any testing or quotation is agreed.
Can testing prove that an entire bulk lot meets a specification?+
Not automatically. The validity of a lot-level conclusion depends on the sampling plan, material variability, agreed criteria and the scope of the analytical work.
Does completing the form book testing or produce a report?+
No. The website prepares an enquiry. Sample acceptance, testing scope, delivery terms and any resulting report require a separately confirmed arrangement.
